jobs.title: Thursday · the week after
jobs.prompt: a four-panel newspaper comic strip, four equal panels in a single horizontal row with thin black gutters (4 panels). Style: comic strip panel, black brush-pen ink line with muddy early-2000s digital flat colors, rubbery kinetic linework, mid-2000s webcomic look, limited palette, slightly misregistered fills. Cast, the same faces, hair and builds in every panel, ages exactly as given: WOOD — aged 26, thin man, hunched, unshaven, tired bloodshot eyes, ink on his right knuckle; GULLY — aged 27, stocky man with a round face, thick forearms, sleeves pushed up; BARNABY (the dog) — a low-slung terrier and hound mix, long body, short legs, folded velvet ears, wiry white-and-tan coat, gray on the muzzle from 2004, cloudy eyes from 2009, carried from 2010. WOOD usually wears black hoodie open over a faded band tee; the brown chore coat outdoors; dark jeans. GULLY usually wears backwards cap, red plaid flannel; the uncle's black rubber apron over it only behind the counter. Clothes, hair-dos and anything held come from this strip's description, never from the reference sheet; hands are empty unless a panel names what they hold. Title of the strip: DRIFT WOOD. The strip: The parody ends. Drift Wood returns. Wood at two-thirds his usual size. Gully, normal. Panel 1: a young man drawn noticeably smaller than normal sitting at a drafting table in an ordinary-sized garage panel, a normal-sized dog beside him, a stack of envelopes with a corporate logo on the floor, muddy digital flats (in this panel: WOOD, BARNABY (the dog)). No dialogue in this panel. Panel 2: a normal-sized young man in a backwards cap standing in a garage doorway looking at a much smaller young man at a drafting table (in this panel: GULLY, WOOD). Gully says "Forty thousand people, Woody.". Panel 3: close-up of a small young man at a drafting table, resigned (in this panel: WOOD). Wood says "Forty thousand people who came for a helicopter.". Panel 4: a garage panel mostly filled by a stack of envelopes on the floor, a normal-sized man in the doorway and a small man at a table not answering, muddy flats (in this panel: GULLY, WOOD). Gully says "Still forty thousand.". Lettering: every balloon and caption contains its complete text exactly as written, in clean hand-lettered comic capitals, large enough to read; size each balloon to fit its whole sentence and never cut a word at a balloon or panel edge; no words other than the ones given. Bottom right margin: tiny signature "A. Finch — Small Wood, OR" beside the gull at two-thirds size (Nov-Dec 2006). Reference @barnaby is the model sheet for BARNABY (the dog): match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Reference @gully_27 is the model sheet for GULLY: match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Reference @wood_26 is the model sheet for WOOD: match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Match the attached references: @barnaby for the character Barnaby; @gully_27 for the character the strip's Gully at 23-31; @wood_26 for the character Wood at 24-31.
